ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.523 ships CLI auth retry, --cwd flag, and tool message
ai.summary: Version 1.0.523 packages a release-candidate-style set of CLI changes from 2025-11-20, including typed error handling with smart React Query retry for auth, a new --cwd <directory> flag passed to initializeApp, and a tool message schema that flattens the content array, moves toolName to the message root, and drops content.output. Other shipped additions include a useTimeout hook for key-based timeout management, reconnection detection with a transient 'Reconnected' status message, useEvent for stable callbacks to prevent unnecessary child re-renders, error display utilities, Ctrl+U visual line delete, and the Hide CLI scrollbar while waiting for response behavior. The agent runtime updates include read_subtree token score remapping for subdirectories, direct tool result push to state.messages, and updated test assertions for the new message content structure.
ai.evidence: The diff shows a single-line version bump in `cli/release/package.json` from "1.0.522" to "1.0.523"; the analysis notes confirm 'Bump version to 1.0.523' and list 16 release updates that this version bump packages.

eli5.text: Freebuff 1.0.523 makes the command-line assistant easier and more reliable to use every day. You can now tell the CLI to work in any folder by adding a --cwd option, so you do not have to navigate there first. When your internet connection drops or your login token expires, the app now recognizes the difference between a temporary network problem and a real credential issue, it will intelligently retry only the temporary errors and keep the login prompt from popping up during network outages. The status bar shows new clear messages like 'Reconnected' when your connection comes back, and it hides the distracting scrollbar while the assistant is thinking. Tool responses now display more cleanly, with new files clearly labeled as 'Create' instead of confusing diff views, and error messages are translated into friendly, readable format when auth or network problems occur. Upgrading means a smoother, less jumpy experience with clearer feedback whenever something goes wrong, so you spend less time fighting the tool and more time getting work done.

If you ran the development command before, you may have seen it silently rebuild the SDK behind the scenes as a fallback; that fallback step is gone, so the dev command starts up directly from the source. The type-checking step also no longer builds the SDK types beforehand, and a few helper scripts and special module declarations were removed since they are no longer needed. This is live today and affects anyone running the CLI in development mode.

For you, the day-to-day user of the assistant, nothing visible changes; the switch simply makes the house’s internal plumbing cleaner and a little less likely to break when engineers update shared code.

eli5.text: When you ask the CLI to send a message and the server doesn't respond (due to a temporary network hiccup or a busy server), the tool now automatically retries the request a few times using an exponentially increasing wait between attempts instead of failing right away. While it's retrying, a small banner appears at the bottom of the status bar letting you know that your message is waiting in line to be delivered. This only affects people running the CLI tool directly on their computer; if you're using a web interface or a pre-built app, you won't see any difference. The retry and banner are part of the live behavior today, not just a setting that's been turned on but unused.

ai.title: Propagate NetworkError in SDK for retry support
ai.summary: agent-runtime re-throws `NetworkError` instead of wrapping it in graceful error output, enabling SDK retry logic to catch it. `promptAiSdkStream` maps `APICallError` status codes and network-related error messages to specific `ErrorCodes` (e.g., `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, `TIMEOUT`, `NETWORK_ERROR`). `run.ts` rejects the promise on retryable errors rather than resolving with cancelled state, and `getRetryableErrorCode` now extracts underlying error types from AI SDK retry failure messages to trigger additional SDK-level retries. Changes affect `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts`, `sdk/src/impl/llm.ts`, `sdk/src/run.ts`, and `sdk/src/index.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant temporarily loses connection to the AI service, it used to give up silently instead of trying again. Now it flags those connection problems as retryable, so the built-in retry system can automatically attempt the request a few more times with short pauses between attempts before giving up. If you are using the SDK to run agents that call AI models, you should see fewer failures caused purely by momentary network hiccups, since the system will now wait briefly and retry instead of stopping on the first failure. This change is live today in the SDK.

eli5.text: When the assistant hits a temporary network problem, it now automatically tries again with a built-in delay, instead of stopping right away. This happens for anyone running the assistant through the software development kit, you'll notice that transient connection errors no longer crash your run, they just quietly retry behind the scenes with a growing wait between attempts. Aborting a run now returns a clean error message instead of throwing one, and the retry settings (like the maximum number of attempts) are applied automatically without extra setup.

ai.title: run() retry logic now handles error outputs
ai.summary: The `run()` wrapper in `sdk/src/run-with-retry.ts` now intercepts `RunState` objects containing `output.type === 'error'` instead of relying solely on thrown `NetworkError` exceptions. This ensures transient failures returned as structured data (e.g., AI SDK 503s) trigger backoff, `onRetry` callbacks, and session state preservation. Tests in `sdk/src/__tests__/run-with-retry.test.ts` verify exponential backoff, abort handling, and `onRetryExhausted` behavior for these output-based errors.

eli5.text: When you run an AI model through the tool, the system used to only retry when it detected a network crash. Now, if the model returns a structured error message (like a 503 service unavailable), it will also retry with a short wait between attempts, up to 1 time by default. You would notice this when using the run() function: instead of failing outright on a transient error returned by the AI service, it will wait a moment and try again, preserving your session state throughout the retries.

ai.title: Fix duplicate agent spawns in CLI
ai.summary: The agent matching logic in `cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts` was updated to prevent duplicate agent spawns. The previous implementation failed to correctly normalize scoped and versioned agent names, leading to mismatches between spawned and stored agents. A new `getBaseName` helper now strips scopes (e.g., `codebuff/`) and versions (e.g., `@0.0.2`) from both event and stored types before comparison. This ensures robust matching across all surfaces using the CLI hook.

eli5.text: Starting today, the CLI assistant will no longer spawn the same team of helper agents twice when you send a message that includes scoped or versioned agent names. The matcher previously compared names literally, so a helper named with a tag or prefix was treated as different from the same helper without one, causing duplicates to start. The matching now ignores those tags and prefixes before deciding whether two names refer to the same helper. You'll notice fewer duplicate processes appearing in your terminal when working with scoped agent names.

ai.title: CLI bash mode and input handling improvements
ai.summary: CLI chat input now supports persistent bash mode triggered by `/bash`, `!`, or typing `!` at start. `router.ts` intercepts commands in bash mode, executing them via `run_terminal_command` and appending `!` to history. `chat-input-bar.tsx` and `use-keyboard-handlers.ts` manage UI state, width adjustments, and Escape-to-clear behavior.

eli5.text: When you interact with the assistant through the command line, you can now type commands directly into your system shell by typing the word 'bash' or an exclamation mark at the start of your message, which keeps every following command running in that shell mode until you turn it off. The input area also hides the mode toggle while you are in bash mode, giving you a little extra room, and pressing Escape clears your current input instead of doing nothing. This is live today for anyone using the command line version of the assistant.

ai.title: Add conservative terminal focus detection for cursor blinking
ai.summary: Implemented XTerm focus reporting to disable cursor blinking when the terminal window loses focus. Added `use-terminal-focus` hook to detect focus states and `isFocusSupported` flag to chat store. Blinking remains disabled until first focus event confirms terminal support. Updated `InputCursor`, `MultilineInput`, and `ChatInputBar` components to respect the new blink state.

eli5.text: When you click away from the terminal window, the blinking text cursor in the input box now stops blinking instead of continuing to flash while the window is unfocused. The app detects whether your terminal supports focus tracking by waiting for a moment when you first click back into the window, and only then enables the blinking behavior; until that first focus confirmation arrives, the cursor stays steady. This affects anyone typing at the command-line chat prompt and using a terminal that reports focus events to the app.

ai.title: Number duplicate implementor agents in CLI
ai.summary: Duplicate implementor agents in the CLI now display sequential numbers (e.g., Sonnet #1, Sonnet #2) to distinguish them. Implementor helpers moved from constants.ts to a new implementor-helpers.ts file, adding getImplementorIndex to calculate numbering based on sibling agent types. message-block.tsx pre-calculates these indices for all nested implementor siblings and passes them to getImplementorDisplayName. Numbering only applies when multiple agents share the exact same agentType.

eli5.text: When the CLI shows you multiple AI assistants of the same type working side by side, they now get labeled with numbers to tell them apart, like seeing "Sonnet #1" and "Sonnet #2" instead of two identical "Sonnet" names. This only happens when more than one assistant of the same kind appears together; a single assistant still shows its plain name. Behind the scenes, the numbering logic was moved into a dedicated helper and calculates each assistant's position among its siblings before the label is drawn. It is live today as part of the CLI.

ai.summary: Replaces static 'Selecting best' text with 'Selected <name>' in CLI agent branch wrapper. Mechanism parses final block's `implementationId` letter to index sibling implementor agents and resolve display name. Refactors `implementorIndex` prop to `siblingBlocks` for dynamic lookup in `AgentBranchWrapper`.

eli5.text: When you run a best-of-N task, the CLI now tells you the actual name of the implementation it picked instead of leaving the line stuck on 'Selecting best'. Once the run finishes, it reads the final implementation's ID letter, maps it back to its sibling agent, and displays that agent's resolved name (for example 'Selected Claude-3.5-Sonnet') in that same status line. You'd notice this only if you were watching the terminal output from a finished best-of-N agent block; it's live wherever the updated CLI (1.0.523) is installed.

ai.title: Add Gemini best-of-n code reviewer for max mode
ai.summary: Internal agent infrastructure adds a Gemini-backed best-of-n code reviewer, replacing GPT-5 in max mode. New files `code-reviewer-best-of-n-gemini.ts` and `code-reviewer-selector-gemini.ts` define the agent and selector, using `google/gemini-3-pro-preview` with medium reasoning effort. `base2.ts` updates max mode to spawn `code-reviewer-best-of-n-gemini` instead of the GPT-5 variant. `createCodeReviewerBestOfN` and `createCodeReviewerSelector` gain a `'gemini'` model option, with `handleStepsGemini` orchestrating n parallel reviews and Gemini selection.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to do a thorough code review (the "max" mode), it now uses Google's Gemini model instead of GPT-5 to compare multiple review suggestions and pick the best one. You won't see any menus change, but behind the scenes the assistant spawns several reviewer agents at once, collects their feedback, and lets Gemini choose which comments to surface to you. This only affects the detailed review step you opted into; everyday, faster reviews are unchanged.

ai.title: CLI 1.0.527 ships bash mode, focus-aware cursor, and best-of-n UI
ai.summary: This release bumps the CLI to 1.0.527 and consolidates several user-visible changes from the same day. Bash mode is now persistent, triggered by `/bash`, `!`, or a leading `!`, with commands routed through `router.ts` via `run_terminal_command` and marked with `!` in history. The cursor blinking state now respects terminal focus via the new `use-terminal-focus` hook and `isFocusSupported` flag. Best-of-N selection now displays the chosen model name and a required one-sentence reason, and duplicate implementor agents are numbered (e.g., Sonnet #1, Sonnet #2) when sibling agents share the same type.
ai.evidence: Commit bb768511 modifies only `cli/release/package.json`, changing the `version` field from `1.0.526` to `1.0.527` (+1/-1 lines).

eli5.text: This release adds a new bash mode for running terminal commands directly from your chat, along with smarter cursor behavior that stops blinking when you switch away from the terminal window. Duplicate AI agents now show numbers (like Sonnet #1, Sonnet #2) so you can tell them apart, and the best-of-n model selector now explains why it picked a particular response instead of just saying 'Selecting best'. When the tool runs multiple AI models and chooses the best result, it tells you the winning model's name and gives a one-sentence reason for the choice. A new Gemini-backed code reviewer is now used in max mode, swapping out the previous GPT-5 reviewer for potentially faster or cheaper evaluations. Upgrading means you get a smoother, more informative terminal experience with clearer feedback whenever the system is weighing or selecting between different AI-generated options.
